what’s special about my plate? 

As a primarily North Indian daughter-in-law, learning to cook traditional South Indian food has been quite an adventure for me. When I first entered my South Indian in-laws’ home, I was introduced to a whole new world of flavors and culinary techniques that were vastly different from what I was accustomed to in my North Indian and global cuisine dominated home! 
Spices and ingredients also vary significantly between North and South Indian cuisines. While we use a lot of garam masalas in the North, South Indian cooking relies heavily on ingredients like curry leaves, mustard seeds and coconut, along with its own myriad of spice mixes. Learning to balance these flavors was a learning curve for me.
Another aspect of South Indian cooking that fascinated me was the variety of chutneys, curries and podis that accompany and flavour meals. Each region in South India has its own unique versions and mastering them has become a point of pride for me.

Over time, I’ve come to appreciate the intricacies of South Indian cuisine and have gained the confidence to prepare dishes like sambar, rasam, and lesser known and commercialised items. It’s been a delightful journey of blending two diverse culinary traditions and creating a harmonious fusion of flavors in our home.

This week’s lunch plate is a reflection of that!
